verdict.rationale: Moneybird documents a terminal CLI and a REST API for your own software. It also offers personal API tokens with selectable scopes, which allow non-interactive, headless authentication suitable for automation. Running it in CI is only implied: the CLI gets a single passing mention, and there are no CI-specific setup docs or hands-on corroboration. Missing for 10: documented CLI usage/flags for non-interactive runs, CI pipeline guidance or examples, independent corroboration of headless/CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Three channels on the same REST API: MCP for an AI chat, the CLI for the terminal, the API for your own software.
Alternatively, you can create a personal API token that simplifies the setup, at a cost of security.
For a personal API token, you can use the checkboxes to select the scopes you need.
